title: Unified Inference: Q1 2027 Product Hub — Overview, PRD, Design, Roadmap, Pricing & Release Notes
author: Priya Shah
content:
Overview

Short intro
This page consolidates the product overview, high-level PRD, core requirements, reference design, roadmap & themes, pricing/packaging notes, and the latest release notes for the Unified Inference product family (hosted API, Dedicated, and Private). It is intended for product, eng, and GTM stakeholders and should be used as the single-source-of-truth for Q1 2027 planning and releases.

1) Product overview

Summary:
- Product name: Redwood Unified Inference (U-Serve)
- Goal: Provide a single, consistent inference API and control plane that delivers predictable latency, cost controls, and operational tooling across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
- Primary users: ML engineers, platform teams, product engineers integrating LLM features.

Key capabilities:
- Text generation and chat with streaming responses and function/tool-calling support.
- Embeddings and reranking endpoints with vector-store friendly payloads.
- Model catalogue with verified performance profiles and automatic fallback routing.
- Cost & latency controls: batching, quantization profiles, prefix/KV caching, and per-route SLA assignments.

SLOs (target for Q1 2027):
- Platform availability: 99.95% monthly for hosted control plane services.
- Inference P95 latency: <= 120ms for small models (<= 4k context) on Dedicated pools; <= 300ms for large models (>= 32k context) where applicable.
- API error rate: < 0.2% 5xx across routes (rolling 30d).

Ownership:
- Product: Priya Shah (product lead)
- Eng: Daniel Kim (serving runtime), Maya Thompson (platform & routing)
- SRE: Luis Garcia

2) High-level PRD and requirements

Objective:
Deliver unified developer experience across deployment modes with clear cost/latency trade-offs and predictable operational behavior for enterprise production workloads.

Primary success metrics:
- Time-to-first-call (self-serve onboarding): < 15 minutes for a sample text-gen flow.
- Mean token cost reduction: 15% YoY via batching/caching and quantization recommendations.
- Enterprise adoption: 25 Dedicated customers onboarded with SLA contracts by EOY.

Functional requirements (MUST):
- FR-001: Single REST/SDK interface supporting text-gen, chat, embeddings, and reranking with identical request/response contracts across deployments.
- FR-002: Model catalogue with metadata: model id, architecture, context window, quantization profile, verified p50/p95 latency on each instance type.
- FR-003: Per-route configuration that allows assignment of: target SLO, max_batch_size, allowed_quantizations, cache_ttl, and fallback model variants.
- FR-004: Rolling canary and A/B rollout tooling integrated with the console and CLI (50% traffic canary policy out-of-box).

Non-functional requirements (SHOULD):
- NFR-001: Provide recommendations engine (Redwood Optimize integration) that suggests batching and quantization to meet user-defined cost/latency targets.
- NFR-002: Audit logs for every model version change, route update, and rollout decision stored for minimum 90 days.

Security/Compliance requirements (MUST for Private):
- KMS integration for private key management (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, customer HSM).
- TLSv1.2+ for all control and data plane traffic, mTLS for Dedicated customer-to-edge connections.

3) Design & architecture (reference design)

Top-level components:
- Control plane (hosted): service for model catalogue, routing policy, billing, rollout, console. Runs in AWS us-west-2 with multi-AZ deployments.
- Data plane (runtime): GPU-optimized inference pods (nv4 family), shard-aware scheduling, kernel selection layer.
- Edge gateway: regional ingress with smart routing by policy (latency, cost, tenant).
- Cache layer: Redis for prefix/KV caching; TTL policies per-route.

Design decisions and rationale:
- Continuous batching: use workload-aware batch sizing to keep latency SLO while improving throughput. Rationale: typical LLM workloads are bursty; batching reduces per-token cost and increases throughput utilization.
- Quantization profiles: support int8 and int4 profiles; recommend int8 for most production workloads, int4 as opt-in for non-critical workloads to lower costs.

APIs & config examples:
- Example route config (YAML):
  ---
  route: "customer-a/chat"
  model: "redwood/gptx-16k-v2"
  sLO_target: "p95:150ms"
  max_batch_size: 8
  allowed_quantizations: ["fp16","int8"]
  cache_ttl_seconds: 30
  fallback_models: ["redwood/gptx-8k-compat"]

- Example CLI rollout command:
  ```
  rwdctl rollout create --route customer-a/chat --model redwood/gptx-16k-v2 --canary-percent 10 --duration 60m --on-failure rollback
  ```

Operational runbook highlights:
1. Degraded P95 latency on route: check autoscaling & batch queue depth, verify kernel selection logs, if sustained, reduce max_batch_size or route to warm Dedicated pool. Owner: runtime oncall.
2. Increased 5xx error rate: check model health, GPU OOM logs, and fallback routing. Activate circuit breaker to failover to a compatible model. Owner: platform oncall.

4) Roadmap & themes (Next 6 months — Q1/Q2 2027)

The roadmap is organized into themes with measurable objectives.

Theme A: Developer experience & onboarding (Q1 2027)
- Goals: reduce time-to-first-call to <15m; add one-click sample apps for embeddings and chat.
- Deliverables: improved console quickstart, SDK examples in Python/Node, templated prompt-sets.
- Owner: Eng Developer Experience (Maya Thompson).

Theme B: Cost controls & Optimize integration (Q1–Q2 2027)
- Goals: release Redwood Optimize recommendations as GA; achieve 10–20% token-cost savings in pilot customers.
- Deliverables: autosuggest quantization profiles, recommended batching configs, per-route cost forecast.
- Owner: Product + Applied ML (Priya Shah + Arjun Mehta).

Theme C: Enterprise readiness & Private deployments (Q2 2027)
- Goals: KMS/HSM integration complete, hardened private control plane packaging, audit-evidence for SOC2 readiness.
- Deliverables: Private 1.0 package, dedicated install runbook, contract templates.
- Owner: Eng Private Deployments (Luis Garcia).

Milestones and timelines (high-level):
- 2027-01-15: Console quickstart and SDK release (beta).
- 2027-02-01: Redwood Optimize GA for recommendation engine (internal customers only).
- 2027-03-15: Private 1.0 packaging and customer pilot.

5) Pricing and packaging notes

Pricing principles:
- Two-axis pricing: compute-cost + managed service fee. Compute-cost is based on model family and instance type (GPU-hour equivalent). Managed service fee covers control plane, routing, and observability.
- Discounts for reserved Dedicated commitments (12/24/36 months).
- Packaging: Self-serve Hosted API, Reserved Dedicated (committed capacity), Private (one-time platform fee + monthly support).

Example pricing tiers (note: illustrative):
| Tier | Compute unit | Price per 1k tokens (gen) | Managed service fee (monthly) | Notes |
|------|--------------|---------------------------:|------------------------------:|-------|
| Hosted (standard) | shared | $0.003 | included in usage | best for dev & small prod |
| Dedicated (reserved) | p3-equivalent | $0.0025 | $1,500 | predictable throughput |
| Private (on-prem) | customer infra | $0.0012 | $25,000 one-time + $2,500/mo support | regulated workloads |

Packaging options & upsells:
- Observability add-on: extended retention, advanced tracing ($500/mo).
- Premium SLA: 99.99% availability and 2-hour incident response ($2,000/mo).

Billing considerations:
- Per-route metering to allow chargebacks by product teams (token and GPU-second breakdown).
- Credits for early adopter pilots (up to 3 months compute credit).

6) Release notes (latest release: 2027-02-01 — Unified Inference v2027.02.01)

Summary:
- Release type: major (product hub + PRD + release notes consolidated).
- Scope: console quickstart beta, SDK updates, Redwood Optimize GA (recommendations), initial Private packaging for pilots.

Notable changes and impact:
- Console quickstart: new onboarding flow reduces self-serve setup to ~10 minutes (includes model selection, sample prompt, and sample integration). Impact: lowers TTFU for new developer users.
- SDK updates: Python and Node SDKs (v1.12) now support streaming responses and function/tool calling parity with REST. Backward compatible with minor config changes.
- Optimize GA: recommendations engine available for internal pilots; suggests batching and quantization with per-route cost/latency forecast.
- Private packaging (pilot): installer, KMS integration hooks, and private control plane docs added. Note: pilot installs require professional services engagement.

Bug fixes:
- Fixed an edge-case where fallback models were not activated when batch queue depth exceeded threshold.
- Resolved an API stability issue that caused increased 5xx rates when switching model versions during heavy traffic.

Known issues & mitigations:
- Large-context model p95 latency can spike under mixed workload conditions. Mitigation: route large-context requests to dedicated warm pools and enable prefix caching.
- Some customers on very bursty traffic patterns may still see suboptimal batching latency; mitigation: per-route max_batch_size tuning and offering burst capacity.

Rollout notes:
1. Beta release will be enabled for internal and pilot customers only for first 30 days.
2. During beta, the product team will run weekly check-ins and collect telemetry on time-to-first-call, token cost, and latency.
3. GA targeted after 30 days subject to performance and stability signals.
